models_evaluated: random forest (compared with gradient boosting, support vector machines, logistic regression)
unlisted_practices: Using a machine learning alarm-prediction model to guide targeted interventions that reduce hemodialysis equipment alarm burden, false alarms, and treatment interruptions (uncontrolled before-after evaluation)

links.outcome: Discriminative performance compared with alternative models
links.effect: Random forest achieved AUC = 0.774, reported as superior to gradient boosting, support vector machines, and logistic regression. Comparator AUCs were not reported.
links.quote: A random forest algorithm was developed to predict alarm events, selected based on superior discriminative performance (AUC = 0.774) compared to gradient boosting, support vector machines, and logistic regression.

links.outcome: Alarm burden, response time, and treatment interruptions after model-guided interventions
links.effect: Uncontrolled before–after comparison reported 43% reduction in total alarm frequency, 56% reduction in false alarm rate, 38% improvement in response time, and 51% reduction in treatment interruptions (all P < 0.001).
links.quote: Implementation of model-guided interventions resulted in substantial improvements across all key performance indicators: 43% reduction in total alarm frequency ( P < 0.001), 56% reduction in false alarm rate ( P < 0.001), 38% improvement in response time ( P < 0.001), and 51% reduction in treatment interruptions ( P < 0.001).

unlisted_practices: Using predictive-model-guided targeted interventions to reduce hemodialysis equipment alarms and treatment interruptions.

links.effect: Predictive model-guided interventions reduced total alarm frequency by 43%, false alarms by 56%, response time by 38%, and treatment interruptions by 51%.
